assessments.classification: core meaning confirmed; remaining bare-form uncertainty
assessments.finding: JUST_JOKING is supported, as is regional Aboriginal English use. The strongest inspected full phrases include just/only; bare gammon may also express disbelief or falseness.
assessments.recommendation: Retain joking concept. A sourced complete just-gammon/just-gammin variant is a sound refinement; do not claim bare gammon is proven wrong or fully certified by these longer examples.
assessments.residual: Exact standalone bare interjection still lacks a newly inspected unambiguous joking-disclaimer example. The regional labels already exist.

assessments.classification: evaluation omitted from generic mapping metadata
assessments.finding: It can refer to a child and can be affectionate; it also carries cheeky/naughty/annoying evaluation. CHILD alone with empty semantic_effects can introduce a judgment from a neutral child trigger.
assessments.recommendation: Retain CHILD-compatible reference and existing vulgarity. Represent the added assessment using the cohesive semantic opinion mechanism; do not relabel every affectionate use as hostile. Parent decides exact metadata/trigger implementation.
assessments.residual: Affection versus hostility depends on relationship and delivery. No evidence here calibrates national commonness or insult default.

assessments.classification: documented extension; current engine routing already narrow
assessments.finding: Current OGLE-only replacements and sex theme already preserve sexual ogling. Australian primary usage independently confirms a joking, admiring look at cars/engines.
assessments.recommendation: No broad LOOK routing correction. Keep or clarify parenthetical gloss as jokingly admiring something, rather than implying any neutral look. Source the extension separately from sexual headword evidence.
assessments.residual: These verb examples do not certify every noun variant or justify removing existing sex/theme policy.

assessments.classification: SAD mapping supported; citation gap closed
assessments.finding: Actual Australian interviews support demoralised/depressed mood. Tired, sick and other flat senses do not contradict this polysemy.
assessments.recommendation: Keep SAD. Add scoped low-mood evidence; avoid deriving exact intensity4 or universal usage from these two contexts.
assessments.residual: One sports quote concerns temporary disappointment and one interview concerns depression; severity calibration remains broader work.

assessments.classification: CONSPICUOUS mapping supported; exact form citation found
assessments.finding: UNSW oral history explicitly uses stuck-out-country-dunny for visible exposure. Alone-country-dunny is another full phrase, not proof this mapping is mistaken.
assessments.recommendation: Keep CONSPICUOUS and cite the exact UNSW utterance. Preserve separate lonely usage if represented elsewhere; do not change this entry to lonely.
assessments.residual: One 2003 recollection establishes use and sense, not widespread current frequency, idiom age, or origin.

assessments.classification: pragmatic context gap, separate from valid response entry
assessments.finding: Independent too-easy response marker is documented; current generic closer has no when constraint. Inspected sources do not show unrestricted content-free sign-off use.
assessments.recommendation: Keep the separate too-easy response entry. Treat unrestricted closer placement as a context-policy question: condition on acceptance/service/acknowledgment signals if the current semantic system supports them, or retain unresolved status until such support exists. No proof of fabrication and no automatic ban recommendation from search absence.
assessments.residual: No full-body generic-farewell attestation found in this focused pass; search failure does not disprove it.

limits: No inferred modern Australian commonness, origin, earliest date, or intensity calibration from isolated usage.
Source independence is grouped by work/event; mirrors are not independent.
